content.thinking:
I'm planning the design: a phoenix perched with wings spread upward and out, talons resting on a small gold-trimmed stone plinth so it reads as grounded while still conveying height. I'll write the whole file in one careful pass without testing, keeping it API-safe.

I'm now working out the geometry: swept capsules for the body, neck, and legs, a sphere for the head with beak spikes and plume crests, and wing bones extending from shoulder to wingtip with fanned feather shapes extruded along each wing's direction.

Still defining wing feather geometry...

I'm reworking the feather fan geometry so it lies properly within the wing plane, with feathers swept along the chord direction (backward along z) and spread outward along the span, deriving perpendicular axes from the span and normal vectors for the extrusion.

Now I'm defining the arm path for the wing, setting shoulder and elbow positions so the wings sweep upward and outward at roughly a 35° angle for a spread pose.

Three feather layers: long primaries sweeping outward and back, shorter secondaries angling inward, and coverts closest to the body. I'm working out length and angle formulas per feather based on position along the arm, plus a gradient color scheme going from deep crimson at the root through gold toward a pale yellow-white tip, evoking phoenix flames.

Defining the feather shape points...

Writing body path and radius...

Writing flame gradient and tail plumes...

Spreading angles from -40 to 40 degrees, with center feathers longer at 1.7 and side ones shorter at 1.2, tilting downward so tips just clear the floor near the plinth base. I'm keeping them straight rather than curled, with the longest tail feathers getting a scalloped flame-like tip for the paint pass.

I'm also planning gold-orange ribbon streamers sweeping back from the tail base in an S-curve, then moving to the head: a scaled sphere for the skull, a golden spike cone for the upper beak angled forward-down, a smaller lower beak, and decal-based anime eyes.

For the eye color I'm weighing amber versus teal against the crimson-orange head, settling on a bright teal like "#2fd6c8" for contrast, placed as a surface decal at azimuth 50 with a small elongated size. I'm also setting up the head's cel-shaded fur edge paint using UV coordinates on the sphere.

Now I'm sketching the facial coloring with countershading between red and gold for the cheeks, and planning a crest made of three plume sweeps curving from the top of the head back and up using catmull paths.

For the glow details, I'm adding a small orange glow orb on the chest like a pyro-emblem, plus a scattering of tiny ember octahedra floating around the creature for extra flair.

Now I'm sketching out the neck curve with a countershaded taper, then building each leg -- thigh, shin, and three forward-pointing talon spikes at the ankle -- so the pose reads as grounded and bird-like.

For the plinth I'm lathing a stone base profile with a cream body and gold rim, adding a thin gold ring sweep around the edge, and planning a rune decal on top for extra detail.

I'm sizing the plinth around radius 0.9 so the tail can trail off its edge, dipping toward the floor near z=-1.5 while staying slightly elevated, giving it a floating, draped feel beyond the base.

Now I'm detailing the wing arm: a deep red sweep with gold bone-like ridges, a gold knob at the wrist, and defining the shoulder-to-wingtip direction geometry using a swept angle to position the wing's endpoint.

I'm computing the feather root positions along the wing arm using vector math, parameterizing the straight sweep path with Vector3 points and direction vectors.

For the primary feathers I'm setting up nine layers with angles sweeping from 25° to 78° off the arm axis and varying their length so the tip feathers taper while mid feathers stay fuller. I'm deciding to build a separate paint per feather since each one is procedural and cheap, rather than trying to share a single atlas.

Now I'm adding secondaries closer to the shoulder, with a tighter angle range and shorter length, and I realize overlapping coplanar feathers will z-fight, so I need to offset each layer slightly along the wing's normal direction — working out that normal via a cross product of the arm direction and the vertical axis to get the correct outward offset.

Once I have the offset direction, I'm stacking layers so coverts sit highest, secondaries in the middle, and primaries at the base, with alternating small offsets between neighboring feathers within a layer so they don't flicker together, then starting to lay out the covert rows with their own length and width parameters.

I'm adding flame-shaped cards along the wing's leading edge using the frame helper, with cards oriented outward and upward for a decorative accent. I also plan to scatter cards across the body and neck surface for added texture.

For the chest ornament, I'm thinking of adding a gold filigree collar around the neck base, likely using a simple torus shape positioned and rotated to follow the neck's angle rather than attempting a more complex surface loop.

Now I'm figuring out the pendant placement by raycasting against the body surface near the chest to find a good front-facing point, then attaching an octahedron gem with a gold setting ring there — accounting for the possibility the ray hit returns null.

I'm deciding against extra tassels and instead planning simpler accents: gold anklets on the shins and a gold circlet torus around the forehead. For the body coloring, I'm setting up a fur-edge cel shader to split orange-red on the back from gold on the belly using a y-axis threshold and a dark red ink outline.

Now I'm picking beak colors—flat gold on top, darker gold below—and deciding wing/arm color can just be a flat red tone. I'm scattering small glowing octahedra as ember particles around the wings, skipping separate streamer ribbons since the tail covers that role, and setting up the tail feather geometry with banded coloring and a central rib running along its extruded length.

Writing feather outline shapes...

I'm laying out nine tail feathers fanned across an angle range with varying lengths and widths, computing each feather's direction and lateral vectors so they splay correctly from the root point, then adding a second shorter, wider layer of covert feathers beneath for depth.

Checking the wing extrusion options (bevel, thickness, orientation vectors) and feather mirroring for left versus right wings, then setting up the eye decal placement, before writing a flame-pattern paint function that blends crimson, orange, gold, and pale colors based on position along each feather.

I'm now worried about whether the shading function passed to `cel` actually receives the surface normal and light sample correctly, since it might crash if that parameter is undefined. To stay safe, I'm computing the shading manually inside the paint function by taking the dot product of the normal with the key light direction and darkening the color with `shadowOf` when it falls below a threshold, while sorting out whether to hardcode the light vector as a plain array.

I should cache shadow colors per base color instead of recomputing shadowOf repeatedly, and write a small toon-shading helper to wrap this logic. I also need to double-check all my imports are actually used to avoid typecheck errors, confirm the default export returns the object3D root from the builder, and verify my path arrays and gradient stops are shaped correctly for the sweep radii.

Now I'm using simplified flat color splits instead of true gradients to reduce risk, and starting to write the wing construction code with vector helpers for the arm sweeps and normals.

Writing wing geometry code...

Still working out feather geometry...

Using the covert layers' luminance to derive feather color values, then checking the leading edge card counts - roughly 80 feather elements across both wings plus tail feathers, all merging cleanly. Now adding the plinth rune texture SVG.

Writing rune ring design...

Placing the plinth and gold ring, then positioning legs and toes atop it, aligning the body along the z-axis to meet the feet naturally. I'm scattering ember octahedrons randomly around the scene while avoiding the figure, then finalizing names, metadata, and writing out the file.

Now I'm constructing the neck, head, and beak geometry using sweeps and spikes, positioning the eyes around the head using angular offsets from its center.

For the crown decoration, I'm figuring out torus orientation—trying a horizontal ring didn't fit the sphere, so I'm testing a vertical hoop-style band instead, deciding on a y-axis torus placed slightly above the head as a gold circlet.

Now I'm sizing the collar torus similarly, aligning its direction with the neck's natural angle and adjusting radius and tube thickness so it hugs the neck properly without being too bulky.

I need to import the right helper functions from toon—furEdge, INK, shadowOf, zigzag, cel—and make sure furEdge nests correctly inside cel calls for the body and head paint without conflicting with shadow-based paints. Then I'm sketching the phoenix's overall proportions: crest height around 2.05+, wings extending up to 2.1.

Wingspan comes to roughly 4.2 meters, which feels oversized for a phoenix, but since it's a fantastical creature I'll let it stand with a body around 1.1 rather than shrinking everything down.
